records.name: SQL Relational NULL
records.equality_behavior: Unknown (NULL = NULL yields UNKNOWN; NULL <> NULL yields UNKNOWN)
records.truthiness: Evaluates to UNKNOWN in WHERE clauses, effectively filtering rows out unless IS NULL is used
records.ordering_behavior: Dialect dependent (PostgreSQL: NULLS LAST by default in ASC; Oracle: NULLS FIRST in ASC; MySQL: NULLS FIRST in ASC)
records.aggregation_behavior: Ignored by COUNT(column), SUM, AVG; included by COUNT(*)
silent_gotchas: WHERE col NOT IN (1, 2, NULL) always returns empty set because col <> NULL is UNKNOWN
Adding NULL to any number yields NULL (col + 10 == NULL)
migration_preservation_rules: In Python, IS NULL must become `is None` or `pd.isna()`
In Python, NOT IN with None in collection behaves differently than SQL

records.name: SAS Numeric Missing Values (. and .A through .Z)
records.equality_behavior: Numeric equality: . == . is TRUE; .A == .A is TRUE; . < .A < .B ... < .Z
records.truthiness: In SAS: 'IF missing_var THEN' evaluates to FALSE (0 and missing values are false; non-zero numbers are true)
records.ordering_behavior: Missing values sort before all negative numbers: ._ < . < .A < .B < ... < .Z < -999999 < 0 < +999999
records.aggregation_behavior: Ignored by SUM(), MEAN(); arithmetic operator (+, -) with missing value propagates missing value
records.serialization_behavior: Often exported as empty string or '.' in CSV/text
silent_gotchas: Critical SAS gotcha: 'IF age < 21 THEN' is TRUE when age is missing! Because . is less than 21.
In Python, if age is None: `None < 21` raises TypeError in Python 3.
migration_preservation_rules: Transform SAS `IF var < X` to Python `if var is not None and var < X` to avoid semantic discrepancy or runtime crash
Map SAS special missings (.A-.Z) to categorical metadata or structured Nullable if code differentiates survey missings

records.name: Python None Singleton
records.equality_behavior: None == None is True; None == 0 is False; None == '' is False
records.ordering_behavior: Unorderable with numbers or strings in Python 3; raises TypeError on < or >
records.aggregation_behavior: None in numeric lists causes TypeError in sum(); handled gracefully by pandas as NaN/None
silent_gotchas: Checking `if x:` treats 0, False, empty list [], and None identically. Use `if x is not None:` when 0 or empty string is valid
migration_preservation_rules: Always use identity comparison `is None` or `is not None` rather than `== None`

records.name: JavaScript null vs undefined
records.data_type_context: null (object type / primitive value), undefined (undefined primitive type)
records.equality_behavior: null == undefined is true; null === undefined is false; null == 0 is false
records.truthiness: Both falsy (Boolean(null) is false, Boolean(undefined) is false)
records.ordering_behavior: Number(null) is 0 (null >= 0 is true, null == 0 is false); Number(undefined) is NaN (undefined >= 0 is false)
records.aggregation_behavior: Array methods handle or skip depending on method
records.serialization_behavior: JSON.stringify() converts null to 'null', but omits keys whose value is undefined
silent_gotchas: JSON.stringify({ a: undefined }) produces '{}'; JSON.stringify({ a: null }) produces '{"a":null}'
typeof null === 'object' (historic bug in JavaScript specification)
migration_preservation_rules: When migrating JS to Python, distinguish between missing key (undefined) and explicit None (null)

records.name: Empty String ('') vs NULL / None
records.equality_behavior: '' == '' is true. In Oracle SQL: empty string '' is treated as NULL! In PostgreSQL/MySQL/Python: '' is not NULL.
records.truthiness: Falsy in Python and JavaScript; truthy in some dialects unless explicitly cast
records.ordering_behavior: Sorts before characters in ASCII/Unicode collation
records.aggregation_behavior: Counted by COUNT(col) because it is non-null in ANSI SQL
silent_gotchas: Oracle SQL treats empty strings as NULL: LENGTH('') IS NULL in Oracle! In Python: len('') == 0.
migration_preservation_rules: Check database dialect: if Oracle migration, empty strings must be normalized or null-checked
